subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 5: Vocabulary and Grammar – Imaginary situations & second conditional
outcomes: Form the second conditional: if + Past simple, would + verb.
Tell real situations from imaginary ones.

tf.s: The second conditional is for imaginary situations.
tf.why: Yes, it talks about things that are not real.

tf.s: The second conditional uses if + Past simple, would + verb.
tf.why: Correct, e.g. If I had a wish, I'd travel.

tf.s: 'If you could travel back in time' is a real situation.
tf.why: We can't travel back in time, so it is imaginary.

tf.s: 'Donate to a charity' means give money to help people.
tf.why: Right, you donate to help others.

tf.s: We say 'If I would have a lot of money, I'd travel.'
tf.why: No would after if: If I had a lot of money, I'd travel.

tf.s: 'I'd' in 'I'd walk on the moon' means I would.
'If you were rich, would you donate to a charity?' is correct.
tf.why: Well done, we use were with you.

tf.s: The second conditional is about things that are always true.
tf.why: That is the zero conditional; the second is imaginary.

tf.s: An inventor is a person who makes new things.
tf.why: Yes, inventors create new ideas and machines.

tf.s: 'Be invisible' means everyone can see you.
tf.why: Invisible means no one can see you.

boxes.q: Complete: If I ___ (go) into space, I'd walk on the moon.
Complete: If you ___ (be) rich, would you donate to a charity?
boxes.why: We use were in the second conditional.

boxes.q: Complete: She'd print jewellery if she ___ a 3D printer.
Choose: They'd feel sad if they ___ the only people on Earth.
boxes.why: No would in the if part: were.

boxes.q: Choose: If I ___ a super ability, I'd like to see through walls.
Which phrase means give money to help people?
A person who invents new things is ...
Real or imaginary: If you could travel back in time?
Complete: If I lived on the moon, I ___ wear a spacesuit.

mcq.q: What is the form of the second conditional?
mcq.why: Second conditional: if + Past simple, would + verb.

mcq.q: When do we use the second conditional?
mcq.why: It talks about unreal or imaginary situations.

mcq.q: What does 'donate to a charity' mean?
Which phrase is NOT an imaginary situation?
mcq.why: Eating breakfast is real and normal.

mcq.q: Complete: If I ___ (live) on the moon, I ___ (need) to wear a spacesuit.

o: If you had a wish, what would you do?
If you would have a wish, what did you do?
If you have a wish, what would you did?
If you had a wish, what will you doing?

mcq.q: Continue the chain: If I became an inventor, ...
o: I'd have lots of good ideas.
I have lots of good ideas yesterday.
mcq.why: Use would ('d) + verb in the result.

mcq.q: Why is 'If I had a lot of money, I'd donate some to charity' a second conditional?
o: It is an imaginary situation with if + Past simple and would.
mcq.why: The speaker imagines having a lot of money.

mcq.q: Which sentence shows a real, possible future, not an imaginary one?
o: If it rains tomorrow, I'll take an umbrella.
If I were invisible, I'd surprise my friends.
If I could fly, I'd go to the Moon.
If I became a film character, I'd be an explorer.
mcq.why: This is a first conditional about a real possibility.

mcq.q: What is wrong with 'If I would be rich, I would travel the world'?
o: We don't use would in the if part; say 'If I were rich'.
We need will in both parts.
mcq.why: The if part uses the Past simple: If I were rich.
